<objective>
Re-skin staff provisioning and device enrolment — the last two of the eight surfaces SC3 names — onto the
Cena design system at the 44px touch floor, with the two destructive confirm dialogs' copy, labels and
ordering byte-identical after the pass.

Purpose: SC3 requires every shipped Phase 01 surface to render in the new system and be usable one-handed
on a phone. Plans 01.1-09 and 01.1-10 covered six; these are the remaining two. They carry two hazards
that are not visual: the destructive dialogs are contracted copy that a re-skin must not touch, and the
devices page is one of the two known sites of the empty-state-gated call-to-action defect, which is why
the ancestor-walking test's table has two rows rather than one.

Output: five re-skinned files, all glyphs on the `Icon` wrapper, no behavioural diff.

**Enabling relationship:** this plan delivers no requirement ID. It completes SC3's eight surfaces.

**The primitives already carry the visual change.** These five files change layout, spacing and
composition only.
</objective>

  <reversibility rating="reversible">A visual pass over the staff list, the provisioning form, the device registry and the two destructive dialogs. The confirmation semantics of the two destructive dialogs are preserved rather than redesigned — a re-skin that made a destructive action easier to trigger would be the one costly outcome on this surface, so the touch floor and the confirm/cancel affordance ordering are held explicitly. No action or authorization path changes. Reversing is `git revert`.</reversibility>
  <action>
    Layout, spacing and glyph routing only, mobile-first at 320px.

    **The staff list.** A row carries an avatar, a name, a role badge and a destructive control. At 320px
    that is a stack, not a table: give the destructive control its own line or a fixed-width column so a
    long name cannot push it off-screen or under the viewport edge. The name renders at the Body role, the
    role badge at Label. Badges are display-only and exempt from the 44px floor, alongside PIN dot
    indicators, non-filter allergen and dietary chips, and the sold-out badge — but the destructive control
    beside them is a control and is not exempt.

    A badge takes **no accent fill**. Accent is reserved for the single primary call to action on a screen,
    the active nav item, active chips and filters, the selected variant row, the "Clear filters" link, the
    focus ring, and a momentary PIN-key press. A role badge is none of those.

    **A deactivated staff member stays on record.** The contracted copy says their past activity stays on
    record, so the row persists in a deactivated state rather than disappearing. Style that state; do not
    filter it out.

    **The empty state** renders the contracted heading, body and call to action from the copy deck. Change
    no string.

    **The provisioning form.** Cena form rhythm: 8px between a label and its control, 16px between fields,
    24px before the submit control. Inputs and the submit control inherit the 44px floor from the
    primitives — verify none is overridden down. Preserve the submit-spinner and disable-on-submit
    behaviour exactly; it is the loading state SC2 depends on. Route the form's glyph through the `Icon`
    wrapper, keeping its existing size and animation classes.

    Change no string on either file. Every user-visible string here is a Copywriting Contract row.
  </action>

    Layout, spacing and glyph routing only.

    **The device registry page.** Device rows carry a status badge, a code and a revoke control; lay them
    out mobile-first at 320px with the same treatment as the staff rows. Status badges take no accent fill.
    Device codes render in `--font-mono` at the Label role — the mono family carries numerics and
    machine-ish strings only (prices, macro values, service hours, table eyebrows, PIN digits, device

    **Do not gate the enable-staff-mode call to action on the device list being empty**, and do not wrap it

    test covers, and it is in that table precisely because the defect shipped twice. The empty state and the
    call to action coexist; the call to action is not part of the empty state.

    **The two destructive dialogs.** Re-skin the layout only. Their titles, their body copy and their
    confirm-button labels are Copywriting Contract rows and must be byte-identical afterwards. Their
    element ordering — title, then body, then the cancel and confirm pair — must not be rearranged for
    visual balance; a confirm control that has moved is a mis-click waiting to happen on a destructive
    action. The destructive confirm control uses the danger token on the danger-soft surface, measured
    5.75:1, and the cancel control stays un-accented.

    Both dialogs inherit focus trapping, the escape handler and focus restore from the Radix dialog

<threat_model>
**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| owner → destructive action | Deactivating a staff member and revoking a device both end access immediately. The confirm dialog is the last checkpoint before that. |
| owner → device enrolment | The enrolment call to action is how a venue gains a new trusted device; a call to action that disappears is an availability defect on a security-relevant flow. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01.1-32 | Tampering | Destructive-dialog copy, confirm labels or element ordering moved during the re-skin | high | mitigate | 01.1 ships no new destructive action. A `git diff` gate asserts no copy reference was added, removed or re-ordered in either dialog, and the ordering — title, body, cancel-and-confirm — is fixed by contract so a confirm control cannot drift under the cursor. |
| T-01.1-36 | Denial of Service | The enable-staff-mode call to action gated on the empty state | high | mitigate | This page is the second of two rows in the ancestor-walking test's table, which exists because the defect shipped twice. The test is run per task rather than once at the end. |
| T-01.1-39 | Elevation of Privilege | Radix focus trapping, escape handling or focus restore reimplemented during the re-skin | high | mitigate | Both dialogs inherit all three from the Radix primitive; the re-skin styles the overlay only and reimplements none of it. A destructive confirmation without a focus trap can be actioned by a keyboard user who believes they are elsewhere. |
| T-01.1-40 | Information Disclosure | A deactivated staff row filtered out of the list | medium | mitigate | The contracted copy states their past activity stays on record, so the row persists in a deactivated state. Removing it would hide an audit-relevant fact behind a visual change. |
</threat_model>
